title: 🔥 "Selective Hearing in the Church: Why Jesus Spoke in Parables to Divide, Not Entertain"
paragraphs:
🔥 "Selective Hearing in the Church: Why Jesus Spoke in Parables to Divide, Not Entertain"
(The Chosen – Season 3, Episode 7: “Ears to Hear”)

Crowds pressed in.
The Teacher sat down.
He opened His mouth—
And instead of clarity,
He told a story.

No explanations.
No bullet points.
Just a riddle… with blood in its meaning.
Why?

Because Jesus didn’t speak in parables to make truth more fun.
He spoke in parables to make spiritual division public.
To reveal who truly had ears—
and who only had curiosity.

The Chosen captured the tone—
But what they missed was this:

The parable wasn’t the message.
It was the measurement.

💭 READER QUESTION:
"Brother John, why would Jesus hide truth from some people instead of explaining it to everyone?"

✅ ANSWER:
Because the Kingdom is not for the casual.
It’s for the surrendered.
And parables separate the surface listeners from the sold-out lovers.

📖 Jesus didn’t make truth more accessible.
He made it more dangerous.

📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE (KJV):
Matthew 13:13 (KJV):
"Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand."

💥 Parables weren’t entry points.
They were filters.
Only those with ears tuned by repentance would decode the fire.
THE CORE TRUTH — WHAT THE BIBLE ACTUALLY SAYS

📖 Key Verse:
Matthew 13:13 (KJV):
"Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand."
✅ Greek Word Breakdown:

Parables = παραβολαῖς (parabolais) — from para (beside) and ballo (to throw).
It means to “throw truth alongside a mystery” —
To mask truth in metaphor, requiring spiritual hunger to decode it.

💥 Parables are not illustrations for clarity.
They are divine riddles — understood only by those who lean in.

Seeing see not / Hearing hear not =
βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν / ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν
This isn’t physical blindness or deafness —
It’s willful spiritual disengagement.

💥 Jesus wasn’t punishing ignorance—
He was exposing hearts that refuse to submit.

📖 Deeper Context: Matthew 13:10–11 (KJV):
"Why speakest thou unto them in parables?"
Jesus answers:
"Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries… but to them it is not given."

💥 Not everyone gets access.
Truth is guarded, not cheap.
Parables were prophetic locks—only opened by surrendered keys.

✅ Hebrew Prophetic Echo — Isaiah 6:9–10 (KJV):
"Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not..."

💥 Jesus quoted this to explain why parables existed.
They fulfill prophecy that some would be in proximity to glory… but still deaf to it.

⚔️ The Word of God always divides:
not between good and bad people,
but between the repentant and the resistant.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, is it possible to hear sermons every week and still have no ears to hear?"

✅ Direct Answer:
Yes.
Hearing without surrender = religious deafness.
Jesus is not looking for listeners.
He’s looking for lovers who obey.

⚔️ Parables were not sermon points.
They were divine tests.
⚡ Summary Strike:

Jesus didn’t hide truth because He was elitist.
He hid it because only the broken should hold it.
If you don’t have ears to obey, you’ll never have ears to understand.
BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF — JESUS SPOKE TO REVEAL HEARTS, NOT TO ENTERTAIN MINDS
📖 BIBLICAL PROOF — PARABLES AS PROPHETIC FILTERS

✅ Matthew 13:10–13 (KJV):
"Why speakest thou unto them in parables? Because it is given unto you to know... but to them it is not given."
💥 Truth:
Jesus used parables to make understanding exclusive—
not because of favoritism, but because of faith posture.
Only those who pressed in would perceive.

✅ Luke 8:10 (KJV):
"Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God: but to others in parables; that seeing they might not see..."
💥 Jesus quoted Isaiah 6:9–10 here — the prophetic root:
Parables were designed to blind the proud, but guide the hungry.

✅ Hebrews 4:2 (KJV):
"The word preached did not profit them, not being mixed with faith in them that heard it."
💥 The Word doesn’t automatically transform—
It divides based on who receives it with obedient faith.
📖 EARLY CHURCH CONFIRMATION — THE MYSTERY OF PARABLES

✅ Origen (184–253 AD) — Commentary on Matthew, Book 10
💥 Key Quote:
"The parables were not spoken to make truth easy, but to make it precious for those who desire it beyond surface things."
🔗 Source: https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/101610.htm

✅ Irenaeus (130–202 AD) — Against Heresies, Book 4, Ch. 26
💥 Key Quote:
"Our Lord, by parables, tested those worthy of the kingdom and left blind those who loved only the surface."
🔗 Source: https://www.newadvent.org/fathers/0103426.htm
📖 HISTORICAL PROOF — RABBINIC METHOD VS. YESHUA’S MYSTERY
Traditional rabbis used parables (mashal) to clarify teachings.
Jesus used them to cloak mystery, revealing only to those with ears of repentance.
💥 This was radical. His disciples had to ask privately what the parables meant. (Matthew 13:36)

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, why does God still allow people to hear truth without understanding it?"

✅ Direct Answer:
Because the Gospel is not about exposure—it’s about response.
Truth becomes clear only after surrender.

⚔️ Parables sort the room.
They’re Heaven’s lie detector.
⚡ Summary Strike:

Parables were never about storytelling.
They were spiritual x-rays — exposing the difference between curiosity and covenant.
OLD TESTAMENT PROPHETIC CONNECTIONS — MESSIANIC ALIGNMENTS

📖 1. Isaiah 6:9–10 (KJV):
"Hear ye indeed, but understand not; and see ye indeed, but perceive not. Make the heart of this people fat..."

💥 Prophetic Connection:
This was the exact scroll Jesus quoted in Matthew 13 and Luke 8.
Isaiah was sent not just to preach truth, but to reveal spiritual deafness.
⚠️ Jesus didn’t invent the parable method.
He fulfilled its judgment purpose — to blind the proud and highlight the hungry.

📖 2. Psalm 78:2 (KJV):
"I will open my mouth in a parable: I will utter dark sayings of old."

💥 Messianic Fulfillment:
This Psalm was a direct prophetic preview of Christ’s teaching style.
Matthew 13:35 says this verse was fulfilled when Jesus taught in parables.
He wasn’t just using a method—He was walking in prophecy.

📖 3. Ezekiel 12:2 (KJV):
"Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of a rebellious house, which have eyes to see, and see not; they have ears to hear, and hear not..."

💥 Prophetic Pattern:
The deafness in Jesus’ crowd was not circumstantial—it was inherited.
Generation after generation heard truth without trembling.
And God used prophets, then parables, then power —
but only the broken ever heard.

📖 4. Deuteronomy 29:4 (KJV):
"Yet the Lord hath not given you an heart to perceive, and eyes to see, and ears to hear, unto this day."

💥 Even in the wilderness, with miracles everywhere,
understanding was withheld—because hearts were proud.
Jesus spoke in parables not to punish but to protect truth from the insincere.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, does this mean some people were never meant to understand?"

✅ Direct Answer:
No.
But it does mean that understanding is given only to the surrendered.
God doesn’t block ears at random.
He closes the scroll to those who refuse to bow.

⚔️ The parable was never a wall.
It was a gate—only the broken found the key.
⚡ Summary Strike:
The prophets saw it.
The psalmists sang it.
Jesus fulfilled it.
And you must respond to it.

If you can hear today—don’t wait.
Because ears harden when hearts don’t obey.
REAL-LIFE TESTIMONY — “THE MAN WHO TAUGHT BUT NEVER HEARD”
⚡ REAL-LIFE TESTIMONY: TYLER — THE THEOLOGY PROFESSOR WHO LOST HIS EARS

Tyler was a brilliant man.
Degrees. Conferences. Applause.
He taught seminary students about exegesis, historical context, and parable structure.

But his life was dry.
No fire. No tears.
Just accurate lectures with no intimacy.
He could quote parables—but he couldn’t feel them.

One night, after giving a talk on the Parable of the Sower,
a student asked him,
"Dr. Tyler, which soil are you?"

He laughed it off.
But when he got home… that question wouldn’t let go.
He opened to Matthew 13, reading it like always—
but this time, something cracked.
"They seeing see not… hearing they hear not… lest at any time they should be converted."

It hit him—he was the hard ground.
He had taught the scroll… but never surrendered to the blade.

He broke down weeping.
Repented.
And for the first time in years—he heard God again.

Now, Tyler no longer teaches with cold intellect.
He preaches with heat.
And every class begins with a warning:

"You can be a scholar of parables…
and still miss the King who spoke them."

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, what if I’ve been hearing truth for years but never truly responded?"

✅ Direct Answer:
Then today is the day you go from auditor to altar.
Jesus isn’t impressed by how much Scripture you can quote.
He’s waiting to see how much you’ll obey.

⚔️ The difference between saved and self-deceived is not knowledge—
it’s surrender.
⚡ Summary Strike:
Tyler didn’t reject Jesus.
He quietly stopped hearing—until the Spirit cut through the silence.
And now, he’s not just teaching parables—he’s living them.
FINAL CHALLENGE — ARE YOU LISTENING, OR JUST LEARNING?

📖 FINAL WARNING — James 1:22 (KJV):
"But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves."

🔥 HEAVEN’S QUESTION TO YOU RIGHT NOW:
Have you become a collector of sermons, but not a responder of truth?
Do you admire parables… or do you tremble under their meaning?

Jesus didn’t speak in riddles to impress.
He spoke in fire-language, designed to test who would press in—
and who would politely tune out.

The Chosen gave us the emotional tone.
But here’s what they didn’t show:

💥 Every parable demands a decision.
And silence… is still an answer.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, how do I know if I’ve truly ‘heard’ God or if I’m just educated by Him?"

✅ Direct Answer:
If it hasn’t changed your walk,
burned your pride,
and brought you to full surrender—
you haven’t truly heard yet.

⚔️ Hearing isn't about soundwaves.
It’s about soul submission.

🚨 FINAL DECISION TIME:
✔️ Bow your heart before the King.
✔️ Don’t just remember the story—repent from the surface life.
✔️ Ask the Lord to give you ears that obey—not just ears that enjoy revelation.

❌ Or stay at a distance.
❌ Keep analyzing truth while avoiding the altar.
❌ Keep scrolling sermons while never trembling before the voice.

⚡ This is your line-in-the-sand moment.
The parable has been told.
The Kingdom is listening.

Will you just hear it?
Or will you live it?
FOOL’S RESPONSE VS. WISE RESPONSE — WHO HEARS, AND WHO JUST LISTENS?

📖 Proverbs 1:5 (KJV):
"A wise man will hear, and will increase learning; and a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels."

⚠️ THE FOOL’S RESPONSE:
❌ “That was a deep message, I’ll think about it.”
❌ “I already know this. I’ve heard it before.”
❌ “Parables are beautiful teachings. That’s all.”
❌ “I’m not deaf. I just don’t feel convicted right now.”

🪓 Result:
The fool treats Jesus’ voice like background noise.
He hears the Word every Sunday—
but it never breaks him,
never alters him,
never moves him.
⚔️ The fool has perfect church attendance… and perfect deafness.

✅ THE WISE RESPONSE:
✔️ “Lord, break the wax of religion in my ears.”
✔️ “I want ears that tremble, not just ears that process.”
✔️ “Every parable is an altar call — I will respond.”
✔️ “I will obey the voice I’ve ignored for too long.”

🛡 Result:
The wise don’t need thunder.
They respond to whispers.
They press in.
They don’t just hear… they hunger.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, what makes someone wise in God’s eyes?”

✅ Direct Answer:
Obedience.
Not intellect.
Not education.
Just raw, surrendered yes when truth pierces.

⚔️ You don’t have to understand everything.
You just have to respond to what you’ve already heard.
⚡ Summary Strike:
One hears to analyze.

One hears to obey.
Which are you?
WHAT IF YOU DIED TONIGHT? — WOULD YOU STAND AS ONE WHO OBEYED… OR ONE WHO JUST LISTENED?

📖 Ecclesiastes 5:1 (KJV):
"Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools..."

💀 ETERNITY MOMENT:
If your lungs collapsed tonight—
Would Heaven say,
✅ “You heard, you trembled, you obeyed.”
Or
❌ “You listened to sermons… but never repented.
You enjoyed parables… but never submitted to truth.”?

Jesus never said,
“He who listens well shall be saved.”
He said,
“He that endures to the end…” (Matthew 24:13)

📖 Luke 8:18 (KJV):
"Take heed therefore how ye hear..."
💥 Because the way you hear
determines the way you’ll be judged.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, I’m scared I’ve gotten comfortable with hearing truth but not living it."

✅ Direct Answer:
That fear means there’s still grace.
But grace is not a delay tool.
It’s a door — and it may not stay open forever.

⚔️ If you died tonight,
you wouldn’t be judged for how many parables you understood—
you’d be judged by the one you refused to obey.
⚡ Summary Strike:

Judgment doesn’t weigh how much you heard.
It weighs what you did with what you heard.

Don’t gamble with soundwaves.
Don’t leave your hearing unconverted.
SATAN’S SNEAK ATTACKS — HOW HELL STEALS YOUR HEARING

👿 1. “You’ve Heard This Before” Familiarity Trap:
"You already know this teaching. Relax."
💥 Truth:
Familiarity breeds deafness.
Every time you hear truth without trembling, your ears harden.
Jesus didn’t repeat truth to fill time — He did it to expose hearts.

👿 2. “Parables Are Just Illustrations” Softening Tactic:
"Jesus was just being creative — don't overanalyze it."
💥 Truth:
Every parable had eternal consequence.
They weren’t illustrations.
They were prophetic weapons, cutting between wheat and tares.

👿 3. “Hearing Is Enough” Passive Religion:
"You’re faithful. You show up and listen — that’s what counts."
💥 Truth:
Hell doesn’t fear hearers.
Hell fears doers.
Satan will let you consume sermons all day — as long as you never respond.
📖 James 1:22 — “Deceiving your own selves…”

👿 4. “God Knows Your Heart” Disobedience Shield:
"Even if you’re not obeying, God knows you still love Him."
💥 Truth:
Jesus said,
“If ye love me, keep my commandments.” (John 14:15)
Love that doesn’t obey is not love.
It’s lip service wrapped in delusion.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, how do I block these attacks from taking my ears again?"

✅ Direct Answer:
Stay broken.
Stay bothered by passivity.
Stay near the altar, not just the crowd.
Pray like Samuel:
“Speak, Lord, for thy servant heareth.” (1 Samuel 3:10)

⚔️ Satan doesn’t mind you hearing Scripture—
as long as it never lands.
⚡ Summary Strike:

The devil’s goal is not to stop you from going to church.
It’s to make sure your ears are numb while you’re there.

He wants you around the Word—
just not changed by it.
GOSPEL WARRIOR DECLARATION — I WILL HEAR AND I WILL OBEY
⚔️🔥 DECLARE THIS OUT LOUD — WITH FIRE, WITH FINALITY, WITH FAITH: 🔥⚔️

"Jesus, I don’t want to just hear You —
I want to follow You.
I don’t want to be moved by parables —
I want to be marked by them.
I reject surface hearing.
I renounce religious deafness.
Give me ears that tremble when You speak.
Give me a heart that bends before You finish the sentence.
I want truth that confronts — not comforts.
I want parables that pierce — not entertain.
I want conviction that produces obedience.
I declare:
I am not just a listener.
I am a Gospel Warrior.
I hear. I respond. I obey.
No more excuses.
No more soft Christianity.
Only fire.
In Jesus’ name — AMEN!"
👉 "I HEAR. I OBEY. I AM A GOSPEL WARRIOR."

Let every devil hear it.
Let Heaven seal it.
Let the scrolls record it.

💭 READER FOLLOW-UP ANSWER:
"Brother John, what if I feel too numb to hear even now?"

✅ Direct Answer:
Cry out louder.
Jesus healed the deaf in Scripture —
He’ll heal your spiritual ears if you ask without pride.

⚔️ Hearing can be restored —
but it starts with humility.
⚡ Summary Strike:
You’ve heard the Word.
Now you’ve declared your allegiance.
This isn’t the end of a blog — it’s the beginning of obedience.
